articleBlocks: Water, Dollar, and Credit Card can make the board feel like it is about payments or monthly expenses. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Appropriation gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Duck is the first hint that the connector is broader than invoices, but it still may not feel locked.
Appropriation is the clue that makes bill unavoidable.
Appropriation bill is such a specific legislative phrase that the rest of the set reorganizes immediately into water bill, duckbill, dollar bill, and credit card bill.
The answer was Words that come before bill.
This board wins by letting everyday money language hide one compound noun and one government term in plain sight.
fullAnalysis: Water, Dollar, and Credit Card all make bill feel possible, but they also tempt you to overread the board as a money or expense theme.
Duck complicates that theory in a helpful way because duckbill uses the same ending in a completely different sense.
Appropriation is the turning clue because appropriation bill is such a formal, fixed phrase that bill becomes much harder to replace with another ending.
Once bill is confirmed, water bill, duckbill, dollar bill, and credit card bill all support it from different contexts.
The answer was Words that come before bill.
The puzzle works because it lets one ending link household payments, legislation, cash, credit, and animal anatomy.
solutionNarrative: Water and Dollar put bill in my head early, but the board still looked like it might only be about money. Duck prevented that from becoming the whole story, because duckbill belongs to a different meaning entirely.
Appropriation made the solve stick. Once appropriation bill clicked, the board stopped being about expenses and became a shared-ending puzzle with one unusual but perfectly fair outlier in duckbill.
